rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed authority disliked one way of referring to the sūra and said one should call it the sūra in which al-Baqara is mentioned.
rows.anchor: وعن بعضهم انه كره ذلك وقال يقال قرأت السورة التي تذكر فيه البقرة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet calls al-Baqara the Qurʾān’s fustāṭ, urges learning it for its blessing, warns that neglect is regret, and says sorcerers cannot master it.
rows.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم 159 ( السورة التي تذكر فيها البقرة فسطاط القرآن فتعلموها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The newborn’s cry supposedly caused by Satan’s touch is figurative imagery of Satan’s eagerness to mislead; literal touching and pricking, as imagined by the ḥashwiyya, is false.
rows.anchor: وأما حقيقة المس والنخس كما يتوهم أهل الحشو فكلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God accepted Mary in place of the male child her mother had vowed.
rows.anchor: رضي بها في النذر مكان الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qabūl may name the means of acceptance: God specially chose her to replace a boy in the vow, although no female had previously been accepted for it, or accepted her immediately after birth before she could serve.
rows.anchor: فيه وجهان احدهما ان يكون القبول اسم ما تقبل به الشيء كالسعوط واللدود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥanna wrapped the newborn Mary, brought her to the Jerusalem temple priests descended from Aaron, and offered her as a vowed child; they competed for her guardianship because of her family’s status.
rows.anchor: وروي ان حنة حين ولدت مريم لفتها في خرقة وحملتها إلى المسجد ووضعتها عند الأحبار أبناء هرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariyyā claimed the right to care for Mary because her maternal aunt was his wife; after the priests refused, twenty-seven men drew lots at a river, and Zakariyyā’s pen floated while theirs sank.
rows.anchor: فقال لهم زكريا أنا أحق بها عندي خالتها فقالوا لا حتى نقترع عليها فانطلقوا وكانوا سبعة وعشرين إلى نهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also reads fa-taqabbalahā as ‘received her at the outset,’ supported by al-Qaṭāmī’s line on taking an affair at its beginning and the proverb about its first occasions.
rows.anchor: قال القطامي ( وخير الأمر ما استقبلت منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proverb خذ الأمر بقوابله likewise supports taking Mary in the first moment of her life.
rows.anchor: ومنه المثل ( خذ الأمر بقوابله ) أي فأخذها في اول امرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good growth is a metaphor for her excellent upbringing, which benefited her in every circumstance.
rows.anchor: مجاز عن التربية الحسنة العائدة عليها بما يصلحها في جميع احوالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has kafalahā on the pattern of ʿamilahā.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( وكفلها زكريا ) بوزن وعملها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the fāʾ doubled and Zakariyyā accusative, God is the agent: He attached Mary to Zakariyyā and made him responsible for her; Ubayy’s akfilhā supports this reading.
rows.anchor: بتشديد الفاء ونصب زكرياء والفعل لله تعالى بمعنى وضمها اليه وجعله كافلا لها

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid reads all three verbs as imperatives, with rabbahā accusative: ‘Accept her, nurture her, and appoint Zakariyyā her guardian.’
rows.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد فتقبلها ربها وأنبتها وكفلها على لفظ الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view takes the miḥrāb as a chamber Zakariyyā built for Mary in the temple, reached by a ladder.
rows.anchor: قيل بنى لها زكريا محرابا في المسجد أي غرفة يصعد اليها بسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes miḥrāb to mean the foremost, most honored place, where Mary was situated in Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: وقيل المحراب أشرف المجالس ومقدمها كأنها وضعت في أشرف موضع من بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view says their mosques were called maḥārīb.
rows.anchor: وقيل كانت مساجدهم تسمى المحاريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariyyā alone entered Mary’s chamber and, on leaving, shut seven doors behind him.
rows.anchor: وروي انه كان لا يدخل عليها الا هو وحده وكان اذا خرج غلق عليها سبعة أبواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary’s provision came down from Paradise; she never suckled, and Zakariyyā found winter fruit in summer and summer fruit in winter.
rows.anchor: كان رزقها ينزل عليها من الجنة ولم ترضع ثديا قط فكان يجد عندها فاكهة الشتاء في الصيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariyyā asks where this unlike-worldly, out-of-season food came from, since the doors were shut and no one could have brought it in.
rows.anchor: من أين لك هذا الرزق الذي لا يشبه أرزاق الدنيا وهو آت في غير حينه والأبواب مغلقة عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is said Mary spoke while still a small child, as Jesus spoke in the cradle.
rows.anchor: قيل تكلمت وهي صغيرة كما تكلم عيسى وهو في المهد

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In a drought, Fāṭima gave the hungry Prophet two loaves and some meat; he returned with a platter miraculously full, asked her this verse’s question, and praised her resemblance to Israel’s foremost woman.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم 169 انه جاع في زمن قحط فأهدت له فاطمة رضي الله عنها رغيفين وبضعة لحم

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشَآءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet gathered ʿAlī, al-Ḥasan, al-Ḥusayn, and his household; they ate their fill while the food remained unchanged, and Fāṭima sent some to neighbors.
rows.anchor: ثم جمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم علي بن أبي طالب والحسن والحسين وجميع اهل بيته فأكلوا عليه حتى شبعوا وبقي الطعام كما هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause ‘God provides’ may continue Mary’s speech.
rows.anchor: من جملة كلام مريم عليها السلام أو من كلام رب العزة عز من قائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ‘God provides’ may be God’s own speech.
rows.anchor: من جملة كلام مريم عليها السلام أو من كلام رب العزة عز من قائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without reckoning can mean provision so abundant it cannot be measured.
rows.anchor: بغير تقدير لكثرته أو تفضلا بغير محاسبة ومجازاة على عمل بحسب الاستحقاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It can also mean gracious provision without accounting or repayment according to earned merit.
rows.anchor: بغير تقدير لكثرته أو تفضلا بغير محاسبة ومجازاة على عمل بحسب الاستحقاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhālika points to the preceding accounts of Zakariyyā, Yaḥyā, Mary, and Jesus: these unseen events were known to the Prophet only through revelation.
rows.anchor: اشارة إلى ما سبق من نبإ زكريا ويحيى ومريم وعيسى عليهم السلام يعني ان ذلك من الغيوب التى لم تعرفها الا بالوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial singles out eyewitnessing because the opponents knew the Prophet had neither listened to tellers nor read their books; denying that he witnessed it sarcastically challenges those who rejected revelation.
rows.anchor: كان معلوما عندهم علما يقينا انه ليس من اهل السماع والقراءة وكانوا منكرين للوحي فلم يبق الا المشاهدة وهي في غاية الاستبعاد والاستحالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He parallels this denial of presence with the statements about not being at the western side, Mount, or when Joseph’s brothers plotted.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وما كنت بجانب الغربي ﴾ القصص 44

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aqlām may mean the lots or arrow-shafts they cast into the river to decide who would care for Mary.
rows.anchor: أزلامهم وهي قداحهم التى طرحوها في النهر مقترعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they were the pens used to write the Torah, chosen for the lot as an act of seeking blessing.
rows.anchor: وقيل هي الأقلام التي كانوا يكتبون بها التوراة اختاروها للقرعة تبركا بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were competing and disputing over who would take responsibility for Mary.
rows.anchor: في شأنها تنافسا في التكفل بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ayyuhum yakful may depend on an implied phrase prompted by yalqūna aqlāmahum: they cast the pens to see, learn, or say who would care for her.
rows.anchor: بمحذوف دل عليه يلقون أقلامهم كانه قيل يلقونها ينظرون أيهم يكفل أو ليعلموا أو يقولون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The addressees are to bear witness to one another’s acknowledgment of the covenant.
rows.anchor: فليشهد بعضكم على بعض بالإقرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s witness to their acknowledgment and their mutual testimony confirms the covenant and warns them against later recanting.
rows.anchor: وهذا توكيد عليهم وتحذير من الرجوع اذا علموا بشهادة الله وشهادة بعضهم على بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the command to bear witness as addressed to the angels.
rows.anchor: وقيل الخطاب للملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘After that’ means after the covenant and its confirmation.
rows.anchor: الميثاق والتوكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāsiqūn here are rebellious disbelievers.
rows.anchor: أي المتمردون من الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repudiating hamza is inserted before the coordinating fa; the sense runs, ‘They are wrongdoers—then do they seek a religion other than God’s?’
rows.anchor: دخلت همزة الانكار على الفاء العاطفة جملة على جملة والمعنى فأولئك هم الفاسقون فغير دين الله يبغون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it coordinates with an omitted clause, approximately ‘Do they turn away, then seek a religion other than God’s?’
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يعطف على محذوف تقديره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object ‘other than God’s religion’ is fronted because the denial is directed especially at the false object of worship.
rows.anchor: وقدم المفعول الذي هو غير دين الله على فعله لأنه اهم من حيث ان الإنكار الذي هو معنى الهمزة متوجه إلى المعبود بالباطل

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: People of the Book disputed before the Prophet over who followed Abraham; he said both groups were clear of Abraham’s religion, and they rejected his judgment and religion, whereupon the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم ( كلا الفريقين بريء من دين إبراهيم )

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads yabghūna with yāʾ and turjaʿūna with tāʾ; both yāʾ forms and both tāʾ forms are also transmitted.
rows.anchor: وهي قراءة أبي عمرو لأن الباغين هم المتولون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those submit voluntarily by considering the proofs and being fair with themselves.
rows.anchor: بالنظر في الأدلة والإنصاف من نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those submit unwillingly under the sword or when confronted by compelling events, such as the mountain over Israel, Pharaoh’s drowning, or imminent death.
rows.anchor: بالسيف أو بمعاينة ما يلجىء إلى الإسلام كنتق الجبل على بني اسرائيل وإدراك الغرق فرعون والإشفاء على الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two words are circumstantial accusatives, meaning ‘willing and compelled.’
rows.anchor: وانتصب طوعا وكرها على الحال بمعنى طائعين ومكرهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase derives from yurīdu Allāhu an yubayyina lakum, with an added lām reinforcing the intent, as in lā abā laka; God clarifies hidden benefits and guides believers along earlier prophets’ and righteous people’s paths.
rows.anchor: أصله يريد الله ان يبين لكم فزيدت اللام مؤكدة لإرادة التبين كما زيدت في لا أبالك لتاكيد اضافة الأب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guides people to acts of obedience that expiate their misdeeds, thereby granting forgiveness.
rows.anchor: ويرشدكم إلى طاعات ان قمتم بها كانت كفارات لسيآتكم فيتوب عليكم ويكفر لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God wills that you do what makes you deserving of His repentance and forgiveness.
rows.anchor: أن تفعلوا ما تستوجبون به ان يتوب عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those following passions want believers to depart greatly from the straight path; no deviation is greater than joining them in lustful conduct.
rows.anchor: وهو الميل عن القصد والحق ولا ميل اعظم منه بمساعدتهم وموافقتهم على اتباع الشهوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view identifies the followers of passions as the Jews.
rows.anchor: وقيل هم اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another identifies them as Magians, who permitted marriage to paternal sisters and nieces; after those unions were forbidden, they argued that Muslims’ permitted kin marriages were no better.
rows.anchor: وقيل المجوس كانوا يحلون نكاح الأخوات من الأب وبنات الأخ وبنات الأخت فلما حرمهن الله قالوا فإنكم تحلون بنت الخالة والعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God lightens the burden by permitting marriage to enslaved women and granting other legal concessions.
rows.anchor: بإحلال نكاح الأمة وغيره من الرخص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings are weak: they cannot patiently resist desires or bear the hardships of acts of obedience.
rows.anchor: لا يصبر عن الشهوات وعلى مشاق الطاعات

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib says Satan never despairs of Adam’s descendants, but approaches them through women; at eighty, despite failing eyesight, he still feared that temptation.
rows.anchor: وعن سعيد بن المسيب ما أيس الشيطان من بني آدم قط الا اتاهم من قبل النساء فقد اتى علي ثمانون سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has the verb in the third person, with its pronoun referring to those who follow passions.
rows.anchor: والضمير للذين يتبعون الشهوات

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reads the verb in the active voice, with al-insān accusative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ( وخلق الإنسان ) على البناء للفاعل ونصب الإنسان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says eight passages in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ are better for this community than sunrise and sunset; the first three are the verses on clarification, repentance, and relief.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ( وخلق الإنسان ) على البناء للفاعل ونصب الإنسان وعنه رضي الله عنه ثمان آيات في سورة النساء هي خير لهذه الأمة مما طلعت عليه الشمس وغربت

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَظْلِمُ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ
وَمَن يَعْمَلْ سُوٓءًا أَوْ يَظْلِمْ نَفْسَهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continuation completes the eight Nisa passages attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās with verses on God’s justice, repentance after sin, and why God would punish the grateful believer.
rows.anchor: و من يعمل سوءا أو يظلم نفسه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās’s account says Ṭuʿma ibn Ubayriq stole Qatāda ibn al-Nuʿmān’s armor in a flour sack, hid it with the Jew Zayd ibn al-Samīn, and was exposed by the flour trail; Banū Ẓafar urged the Prophet to defend Ṭuʿma and blame the Jew, prompting this revelation.
rows.anchor: ذكره الثعلبي من رواية أبي صالح عن الكلبي عن ابن عباس ونقله الواحدي في الاسباب عن المفسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭuʿma fled to Mecca, apostatized, and later died when a wall collapsed on him as he broke into a house to steal.
rows.anchor: وروي ان طعمة هرب إلى مكة وارتد ونقب حائطا بمكة ليسرق اهله فسقط الحائط عليه فقتله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God showed the Prophet means what He made him know and revealed to him.
rows.anchor: بما عرفك واوحى به اليك

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: ʿUmar warns others not to claim their judgments are what God showed them: only the Prophet had divinely guided judgment, while others rely on conjecture and effort.
rows.anchor: وعن عمر رضي الله عنه لا يقولن احدكم قضيت بما اراني الله فإن الله لم يجعل ذلك الا لنبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told not to litigate for traitors against the innocent, specifically not to defend Banū Ẓafar against the Jew.
rows.anchor: ولا تكن لأجل الخائنين مخاصما للبراء يعني لا تخاصم اليهود لأجل بني ظفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to seek forgiveness concerns the Prophet’s intention to punish the Jew.
rows.anchor: مما هممت به من عقاب اليهودي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s favor and mercy mean His protection, gracious care, and revelation that exposed the group’s secret.
rows.anchor: أي عصمته وألطافه وما اوحى اليك من الاطلاع على سرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The group trying to mislead the Prophet is from Banū Ẓafar.
rows.anchor: من بني ظفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They wanted to turn him from a just ruling although they knew their own man was guilty; some knew the full facts.
rows.anchor: عن القضاء بالحق وتوخي طريق العدل مع علمهم أن الجاني هو صاحبهم فقد روي ان ناسا منهم كانوا يعلمون كنه القصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their attempt harms only themselves because its consequences fall back on them.
rows.anchor: لأن وباله عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They do not harm the Prophet: he acted on the outward evidence and had no reason to suspect the facts were otherwise.
rows.anchor: لأنك انما عملت بظاهر الحال وما كان يخطر ببالك ان الحقيقة على خلاف ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What the Prophet had not known may be hidden events and people’s inner thoughts, or matters of religion and revealed law.
rows.anchor: من خفيات الأمور وضمائر القلوب أو من امور الدين والشرائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the group is Banū Ẓafar, minhum refers to them; another view identifies the group as hypocrites and takes minhum to refer to the people generally.
rows.anchor: ويجوز ان يراد بالطائفة بنو ظفر ويرجع الضمير في ( منهم ) إلى الناس وقيل الآية في المنافقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account identifies the two sons as Cain and Abel: Adam paired each twin with the other, but Cain envied Abel because his own twin Iqlīmā was more beautiful; fire consumed Abel’s offering, and Cain threatened him.
rows.anchor: هما ابنا آدم لصلبه قابيل وهابيل اوحى الله إلى آدم أن يزوج كل واحد منهما توأمه الآخر وكانت توامة قابيل اجمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says the two men were Israelites, not Adam’s sons.
rows.anchor: وقيل هما رجلان من بني اسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bi-l-ḥaqq may mean recite an account marked by truth and soundness.
rows.anchor: تلاوة ملتبسة بالحق والصحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may mean an accurate account agreeing with the earlier scriptures.
rows.anchor: أو اتله نبأ ملتبسا بالصدق موافقا لما في كتب الأولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may refer to the proper aim of condemning envy, since polytheists and the People of the Book envied and opposed the Prophet.
rows.anchor: أو بالغرض الصحيح وهو تقبيح الحسد لأن المشركين واهل الكتاب كلهم كانوا يحسدون رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading means: tell them the account while being truthful and in the right.
rows.anchor: أو اتل عليهم وانت محق صادق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time clause may be governed by al-nabaʾ, meaning their story at that time.
rows.anchor: نصب بالنبأ أي قصتهم وحديثهم في ذلك الوقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is apposition to al-nabaʾ, with an omitted annexed noun: ‘the news of that time.’
rows.anchor: ويجوز ان يكون بدلا من النبأ أي اتل عليهم النبأ نبأ ذلك الوقت على تقدير حذف المضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurbān is what one uses to draw near to God, such as a sacrifice or charity, just as ḥulwān is something given.
rows.anchor: والقربان اسم ما يتقرب به إلى الله من نسيكة أو صدقة كما ان الحلوان اسم ما يحلى

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī notes that taqarraba is made transitive with bi- to mean qarraba, ‘to bring near.’
rows.anchor: قال الأصمعي تقربوا قرب القمع فيعدى بالباء حتى يكون بمعنى قرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because envy over the accepted offering provoked the death threat, Abel answers that Cain’s failure stems from abandoning piety, not from Abel; he should blame and reform himself.
rows.anchor: لما كان الحسد لأخيه على تقبل قربانه هو الذي حمله على توعده بالقتل قال له إنما أتيت من قبل نفسك لانسلاخها من لباس التقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that God accepts obedience only from a believing, God-fearing person, a warning to many who perform works.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على ان الله تعالى لا يقبل طاعة الا من مؤمن متق فما أنعاه على اكثر العاملين اعمالهم

rows.speaker: عامر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: At death, ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Allāh wept and explained that he heard God say acceptance belongs to the God-fearing.
rows.anchor: وعن عامر بن عبد الله انه بكى حين حضرته الوفاة فقيل له ما يبكيك فقد كنت وكنت قال إني أسمع الله يقول

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid and others say Abel was stronger but refrained and surrendered from fear of God, since self-defense was not permitted under that law.
rows.anchor: قيل كان أقوى من القاتل وأبطش منه ولكنه تحرج عن قتل أخيه واستسلم له خوفا من الله لأن الدفع لم يكن مباحا في ذلك الوقت قاله مجاهد وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abel means that Cain would bear the consequence of killing him as well as his own sin; using ‘my sin’ expansively means its like, as in ‘I read his reading.’
rows.anchor: أن تحتمل إثم قتلي لك لو قتلتك وإثم قتلك لي

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The sound report says that the two who trade insults incur what they say, with the initiator bearing the blame unless the wronged party exceeds the limit; the initiator caused the answering insult.
rows.anchor: ونحوه قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام 347 ( المستبان ما قالا فعلى البادي ما لم يعتد المظلوم ) + صحيح +

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Abel did not kill or defend himself, his stated sin is conditional and estimated: what he would have incurred had he struck first.
rows.anchor: هو مقدر فهو يحتمل مثل الإثم المقدر كأنه قال إني أريد ان تبوء بمثل إثمي لو بسطت يدي إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes ‘my sin’ as the sin of killing me and ‘your sin’ as the sin that caused your sacrifice to be rejected.
rows.anchor: وقيل ( بإثمي ) بإثم قتلي ( وإثمك ) الذي من اجله لم يتقبل قربانك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abel may wish a tyrant to receive just punishment: what is good may be willed by God and by a servant.
rows.anchor: كان ظالما وجزاء الظالم حسن جائز ان يراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To the objection that no bearer carries another’s burden, he answers that ‘my sin’ means its equivalent, an established expansive idiom.
rows.anchor: فإن قلت كيف يحمل إثم قتله له ولا تزر وازرة وزر اخرى قلت المراد بمثل إثمي على الاتساع في الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoer’s just punishment is good; since God may will it, a servant may will it too, because he wills only what is good.
rows.anchor: وإذا جاز ان يريده الله جاز ان يريده العبد لأنه لا يريد الا ما هو حسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional uses a verb but its answer uses a nominal participle to convey that Abel will not do an act that earns the vile description; the bāʾ reinforces the negation.
rows.anchor: ليفيد انه لا يفعل ما يكتسب به هذا الوصف الشنيع ولذلك أكده بالباء المؤكدة للنفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His soul made the murder seem easy and wide open, from the idiom for pasture that has spread out.
rows.anchor: فوسعته له ويسرته من طاع له المرتع اذا اتسع

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads fa-ṭāwaʿat; it may be a form-IV verb with the sense of faʿala, or mean that the murder called to Cain and his soul complied.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ( فطاوعت ) وفيه وجهان ان يكون مما جاء من فاعل بمعنى فعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says Cain killed Abel at age twenty, either at ʿAqabat Ḥirāʾ or at Baṣra where the Great Mosque stands.
rows.anchor: وقيل قتل وهو ابن عشرين سنة وكان قتله عند عقبة حراء وقيل بالبصرة في موضع المسجد الأعظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first human killing left Cain unable to bury Abel; after carrying the body in a sack for a year, he saw two ravens fight, one kill the other, dig a grave with beak and feet, and bury it.
rows.anchor: ولما قتله تركه بالعراء لا يدري ما يصنع به فخاف عليه السباع فحمله في جراب على ظهره سنة حتى أروح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says Cain’s formerly white body turned black after the killing, and Adam accused him when Cain denied being his brother’s keeper.
rows.anchor: ويروى انه لما قتله اسود جسده وكان أبيض فسأله آدم عن اخيه فقال ما كنت عليه وكيلا فقال بل قتلته ولذلك اسود جسدك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tale that Adam stopped laughing for a hundred years and mourned Abel in verse is sheer falsehood; the poem is fabricated and ungrammatical, and prophets are protected from poetry.
rows.anchor: وروي ان آدم مكث بعد قتله مائة سنة لا يضحك وانه رثاه بشعر وهو كذب بحت وما الشعر الا منحول ملحون وقد صح أن الأنبياء عليهم السلام معصومون من الشعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject may be God, who showed Cain, or the raven; the raven is figuratively treated as intending to teach because it caused the lesson.
rows.anchor: ليريه الله أو ليريه الغراب أي ليعلمه لأنه لما كان سبب تعليمه فكأنه قصد تعليمه على سبيل المجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawʾah can mean the shameful exposed part of Abel’s body, which should not be uncovered.
rows.anchor: عورة أخيه وما لا يجوز ان ينكشف من جسده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawʾah can also mean disgrace because of its ugliness; the cited poetic cry uses it for a terrible scandal.
rows.anchor: قال ( يا لقوم للسوأة السواء ) أي للفضيحة العظيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-uwāriya may be subjunctive as the answer to the question, indicative with an omitted ana, or subjunctive with its ending lightened.
rows.anchor: بالنصب على جواب الاستفهام وقرىء بالسكون على فأنا اواري أو على التسكين في موضع النصب للتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cain regretted the killing because carrying the body exhausted him, he was perplexed and helpless, had to learn from the raven, his color changed, and his father was angry; he did not repent as a penitent does.
rows.anchor: على قتله لما تعب فيه من حمله وتحيره في امره وتبين له من عجزه وتلمذه للغراب واسوداد لونه وسخط أبيه ولم يندم ندم التائبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min ajli dhālika means ‘because of that’; the expression is linked to ajala, to incur or bring about a thing, as in min jarāka.
rows.anchor: بسبب ذلك وبعلته وقيل أصله من أجل شرا اذا جناه يأجله أجلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The min in min ajli marks the starting point: the commandment’s institution began because of that killing.
rows.anchor: لابتداء الغاية أي ابتدأ الكتب ونشأ من اجل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading drops the hamza and transfers its fatḥa to nūn; Abū Jaʿfar reads with kasra on the hamza, transferred to nūn when lightened.
rows.anchor: بحذف الهمزة وفتح النون لالقاء حركتها عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bi-ghayri nafs means without killing a person in lawful retaliation.
rows.anchor: بغير قتل نفس لا على وجه الاقتصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fasād is coordinated with nafs, so the phrase means without a life or without corruption.
rows.anchor: عطف على نفس بمعنى أو بغير فساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The corruption on earth may mean associating partners with God.
rows.anchor: وهو الشرك وقيل قطع الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it may mean highway robbery.
rows.anchor: وهو الشرك وقيل قطع الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saving a life includes rescuing someone from murder, drowning, fire, a collapse, or another cause of death.
rows.anchor: ومن استنقذها من بعض أسباب الهلكة قتل أو غرق أو حرق أو هدم أو غير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One person equals all people in sanctity because every human shares honor before God; the comparison magnifies killing and saving life, deterring attacks and encouraging protection.
rows.anchor: لأن كل إنسان يدلي بما يدلي به الآخر من الكرامة على الله وثبوت الحرمة فإذا قتل فقد أهين ما كرم على الله وهتكت حرمته وعلى العكس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says a killer faces Hell, God’s wrath, and immense punishment; killing everyone would add nothing beyond that.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد قاتل النفس جزاؤه جهنم وغضب الله والعذاب العظيم ولو قتل الناس جميعا لم يزد على ذلك

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan tells the killer of even one person that, just as killing all people would leave no deed to balance it for forgiveness, one killing is the same deception of the self and Satan.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن يا ابن آدم أرأيت لو قتلت الناس جميعا اكنت تطمع ان يكون لك عمل يوازي ذلك فيغفر لك به كلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘After that’ means after the commandment was written and after messengers came with signs.
rows.anchor: بعدما كتبنا عليهم وبعد مجيء الرسل بالآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelites are extravagant in killing and do not regard its gravity.
rows.anchor: يعني في القتل لا يبالون بعظمته

words: إِنَّمَا وَلِيُّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After forbidding allegiance to those who must be opposed, the passage names those who must be allied.
rows.anchor: عقب النهي عن موالاة من تجب معاداتهم ذكر من تجب موالاتهم بقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Innamā makes allegiance to God, His Messenger, and believers exclusive and obligatory.
rows.anchor: ومعنى ( إنما ) وجوب اختصاصهم بالموالاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular walī begins with God’s intrinsic guardianship, then adds the Prophet and believers derivatively; using plural awliyāʾ would erase this distinction between origin and dependent status.
rows.anchor: أصل الكلام إنما وليكم الله فجعلت الولاية لله على طريق الأصالة ثم نظم في سلك اثباتها له إثباتها لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والمؤمنين على سبيل التبع

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh’s reading has mawlākum.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله ( إنما مولاكم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alladhīna yuqīmūna may be nominative as an appositive to alladhīna āmanū, a predicate of an implied ‘they are,’ or accusative as praise.
rows.anchor: الرفع على البدل من الذين آمنوا أو على هم الذين يقيمون أو النصب على المدح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description distinguishes sincere believers from hypocrites and from those whose hearts assent but whose deeds fall short.
rows.anchor: وفيه تمييز للخلص من الذين آمنوا نفاقا أو واطأت قلوبهم ألسنتهم الا انهم مفرطون في العمل
